clue.text: Drink to accompany buns and toast

indicators.note: one thing accompanying another goes along beside it, so the drink sits right after the buns

parts.note: buns is slang for the buttocks, the bottom
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone orders something to wash down their buns and toast at a café.
explanation.walkthrough: Buns and toast look like a breakfast plate, but buns is the rear end and toast is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: BOTTOMS UP is the cheery phrase said when raising glasses before drinking together.

clue.text: Full of himself, he aged badly overwhelmed by venture

indicators.note: being overwhelmed means being engulfed, so these letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: a bid is an attempt or venture

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A conceited man ages poorly after being swamped by a risky business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bigheaded is conceited, with an inflated opinion of his own importance.

clue.text: Irritable cops doubt witness

indicators.note: to cop is to catch or grab hold of, so the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: testy means irritable or short-tempered
an if is a doubt or condition, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Bad-tempered police officers distrust what a witness tells them.
explanation.walkthrough: Cops looks like the police, but here it is a verb meaning catches.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something formally is to testify, giving evidence or bearing witness to it.

clue.text: Oxygen given by doctor at home birth

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
to doctor results is to rig or falsify them
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A doctor supplies oxygen during a home birth.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor is a verb here, meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Birth can mean beginning or source, as in the birth of an idea, which is an origin.

clue.text: Function announced for board (for information)

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we go by how the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A post on an information board is advertised for some function or event.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a panel or noticeboard put up to give people directions or information.

clue.text: Saleswoman reflects pretty clothing is benefit of the job

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: clothing wraps around a body, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: pretty good means quite good
taken as written

explanation.surface: A saleswoman muses that pretty clothes are one of her job's perks.
explanation.walkthrough: Pretty is an adverb meaning fairly, not an adjective describing the clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A perquisite, or perk, is an extra advantage that comes with employment beyond pay.

clue.text: Conviction for arson inevitably troubles Haberdashers' principals

indicators.note: principals are the leaders or heads, so we take the opening letter of each word

parts.note: the leading letters of five words

explanation.surface: An arson conviction is bad news for the heads of a livery company of cloth merchants.
explanation.walkthrough: Principals, spelt this way, means head teachers or chiefs; Haberdashers' is a London livery company with schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith is firm belief or conviction, especially in something without proof.

clue.text: Enthusiastic groups spread out near woods?

parts.note: to fan out is to spread out
woods are a kind of golf club, so they are clubs by example, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Groups of enthusiasts spread out near a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Fan clubs are organised associations of devoted admirers of a performer or team.

clue.text: Witless old Ugandan, informally in charge, clutching religious texts

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold tightly, so the outer letters grip something between them

parts.note: Idi Amin, former Ugandan dictator, known by his first name
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A foolish former Ugandan leader holds sacred books.
explanation.definitionFit: Witless means lacking sense or intelligence, which is exactly what idiotic describes.

clue.text: One who fishes in Rother only

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only one person goes angling on the River Rother.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rother is a river in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-legged wading bird catches its food by spearing fish in shallow water.

clue.text: Try to suspend youngster often found in lake

parts.note: to have a go is to try
to sling is to hang or suspend

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to hang up a young person discovered in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A gosling is a baby goose, a young bird commonly seen paddling on lakes and ponds.

clue.text: Managed to decline bite of rendang (it's relatively hot)

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
to die away is to decline or fade

indicators.note: a bite is a small first taste, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: rendang is a spicy Indonesian beef curry

explanation.surface: Someone manages to refuse a mouthful of rendang, the curry being rather spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot here means sexually aroused, not spicy; relatively signals the comparative form.
explanation.definitionFit: Randier is the comparative of randy, meaning more lustful, and hot is slang for aroused.

clue.text: Bring out Israeli citizens' sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between two slices, so the answer is held within these words

parts.note: the letters span the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone lays out sandwiches made by Israeli citizens.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a response is to draw it out or evoke it from someone.

clue.text: Nonsense regularly left in news round-up …

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rubbish keeps getting left in the news summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short broadcast or printed summary of the latest news.

clue.text: After a wash, it helps fool roaming sheep back in outbuilding

parts.note: a clot is a stupid person

indicators.note: roaming animals wander about, so these letters stray from their usual order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: the back of a word is its tail, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: After dipping, a farmhand fools around with wandering sheep in a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: A sheep wash suggests the farmyard, but the wash is laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Once laundry is washed, a clothes peg helps by clipping garments to the line to dry.

clue.text: … in Times — bewilderment reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: a daze is a state of bewilderment

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: confusion is described in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins the surface to the previous clue; Times looks like the newspaper but means periods.
explanation.definitionFit: Days can mean an era or period, as in the old days, the same as times gone by.

clue.text: Reminders of past show-offs on the rugby pitch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: scenes recalling earlier events
second meaning, playful: flamboyant players in the back line of a rugby team

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into flash, meaning showy, and backs, the rugby positions behind the forwards; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashbacks are sudden vivid memories or film scenes that return to earlier events.

clue.text: Careless partner's overturned hot waste container, displacing lid

indicators.note: something overturned is turned upside down, so in a down entry it reads the other way
displacing the lid pushes out the top letter and puts another in its place

parts.note: a pal is a partner or mate, with the possessive s
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a nappy is a diaper, which contains a baby's waste

explanation.surface: A partner knocks over a bin of hot rubbish, sending its lid flying.
explanation.walkthrough: H takes the place of the opening N; a nappy is the British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaphappy describes a casual, cheerfully irresponsible attitude, which is careless.

clue.text: Indecent to drop trousers for a rare sighting?

parts.note: blue jokes are indecent or smutty
to moon is to bare your backside as a prank

explanation.surface: Pulling down your trousers in public is indecent, but rarely seen.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a play on the idiom once in a blue moon, meaning hardly ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue moon is a second full moon in one calendar month, an uncommon event in the sky.

clue.text: Make weak tea clumsily after young woman gets one drunk

indicators.note: after places one part behind the other, so the jumbled letters come last

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young upper-class woman

indicators.note: doing something clumsily makes a mess of it, so the letters come out muddled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
lit is slang for drunk
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl brews weak tea badly after someone gets her drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To debilitate is to sap someone's strength or energy, leaving them feeble.

clue.text: Ultimately, cars unable to travel here

definitions.text: Ultimately, cars unable to travel here

indicators.note: letters that travel move around, so they are rearranged
ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: In the end, cars are not permitted to drive in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: cars may not use a lane reserved for buses.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus lane is a road lane reserved for buses, where ordinary cars are forbidden to drive.

clue.text: Every now and then, middleman offers a thought

indicators.note: something happening every now and then occurs at intervals, so we take every other letter

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Occasionally a go-between puts forward a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a notion or concept formed in the mind, which is what a thought is.

clue.text: Scheme spread assistance around

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so in a down entry the letters run upward

parts.note: marg is short for margarine, a spread
aid means help or assistance

explanation.surface: A programme distributed help widely.
explanation.walkthrough: Spread looks like a verb but is the noun for something put on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme can be a plan or chart showing how parts are arranged, as a diagram does.

clue.text: Hospital department probing recalled boy's concerning teeth

indicators.note: a probe pushes into something, so the first part goes inside the other
recalling means calling back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A hospital department investigates a returned boy's tooth trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental is the adjective for matters relating to the teeth and their care.

clue.text: Bill's reliant on one meagre business concept finally flying

indicators.note: letters sent flying scatter and land in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so the closing letters of the two words are used

parts.note: the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: Bill is staking everything on a single thin business idea taking off.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name but is an invoice: a gas bill depends on the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A household gas bill is calculated from the consumption recorded by the meter.

clue.text: Good copy — the initiator of superior openings

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to ape is to copy or mimic

indicators.note: an initiator starts things off, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A good imitation comes from whoever started a better beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Gapes are wide openings or gaps, from the verb meaning to open wide.

clue.text: Angelic character's turn of phrase

indicators.note: a turn moves things round, so the following word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A sweet-natured person has a lovely way with words.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn of phrase is a stock idiom; here it is split into an instruction and its material.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of angels, so it is a heavenly being.

clue.text: Square little room lacking in taste

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so these letters are removed from the other word

parts.note: flavour is taste
lav is short for lavatory, a small room

explanation.surface: A small, cosy room with no style at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Square means a number multiplied by itself: two squared is four.
explanation.definitionFit: Four is the square of two, so it is a square number in arithmetic.

clue.text: Spooner's to take in crap liquid lunch, perhaps

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the starting sounds of words

parts.note: to take in a view is to see it, and poop is crap

explanation.surface: Someone is told to swallow rubbish and call it a liquid lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of see and poop yields the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea soup is a broth that might well be served at midday; perhaps flags it as an example.

clue.text: Sudden appearance of the King immersed in public work

indicators.note: something immersed is plunged inside, so these letters go within the others

parts.note: news that is out is public
op is short for opus, a work
CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles

explanation.surface: A king's surprise turn in a public works project.
explanation.walkthrough: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop, like an outbreak, can mean a sudden emergence or showing of something.

clue.text: Rear small bird

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tern is a seabird

explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the back part of a ship, so it is the rear of the vessel.

clue.text: Seriously distasteful to eat black fruit

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the outer word swallows the others

parts.note: gory scenes are bloody and distasteful
B is the pencil abbreviation for black
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Someone finds it truly unpleasant to eat dark fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Seriously is the exclamation of disbelief, not an adverb qualifying distasteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorblimey is a Cockney exclamation of astonishment, like saying Seriously! in disbelief.
